key_insight: Co-PiLOT combines a learned generative latent space with physics-informed Bayesian optimization to make expensive inverse design feasible under strong validity and constraint requirements.
engineering_relevance: This enables target-driven microstructure design for solid mechanics by searching in a compact latent space while preserving manufacturable, solver-compatible candidates.
method: Train a ViT-based encoder with latent diffusion / DiT / rectified-flow decoders on ~80,000 EBSD microstructure images.
Use the decoder as a validity prior and a self-segmenting orientation codec to convert decoded images into crystal plasticity solver inputs.
Optimize in latent space with MERIDIAN: deep-kernel GP uncertainty, feasibility prediction, manifold-aware trust regions, and target-aware acquisition.
evidence_signal: On a budget of 160 simulations, the ViT-FMDiT + MERIDIAN setup achieved the best target-driven objective and cut relative target error by 3–22% versus seven baselines.
watch_item: Performance depends on the learned decoder and latent-space quality, so dataset bias or decoding errors can limit transferability to new microstructures or constraints.
paper_title: Co-PiLOT: Constrained Physics-Informed Latent Optimization for Target-Driven Inverse Design
